scope: All 49 findings from the 2026-11-03 source audit

items.subject: Crossterm event-stream
items.resolution: Remove unused async event-stream feature; Events uses poll/read on its owned thread.

items.subject: Unused failed-platform selection
items.resolution: Remove failed_platform and its obsolete dedicated test; retry selection uses explicit platform or the release default.

items.subject: Unused retry root argument
items.resolution: Remove the unused repository-root parameter.

items.subject: Legacy build_jobs wrapper
items.resolution: Use build_jobs_for in both production and scheduling tests.

items.subject: Application identity entry points
items.resolution: Use ApplicationIdentity::capture with an explicit ApplicationScope in production and tests.

items.subject: Linux installer test wrapper
items.resolution: Production and tests use the same parameterized package installer.

items.subject: Service convenience APIs
items.resolution: Public convenience APIs delegate to the cancellable implementation; repository-only references do not establish absence of external users.

items.subject: Operations convenience APIs
items.resolution: Public in-memory editing and explicit local validation are distinct from Store persistence.

items.subject: Image convenience APIs
items.resolution: Public wrappers deliberately provide default limits and bounds; preserve their external contract.

items.subject: Explicit configuration and trust APIs
items.resolution: Explicit settings avoid process-global environment mutation; design-only trust revocation differs from revoking all project grants.

items.subject: Store lock APIs
items.resolution: Expose the shared lock protocol to integration users; cancellation-free wrappers share the same implementation.

items.subject: Runtime injection and diagnostic APIs
items.resolution: Custom executables, embedded-host supervisors and owned-process diagnostics have documented independent purposes.

items.subject: Authentication-only API
items.resolution: Public account inspection intentionally avoids sessions, tools, login and prompts; its branch is reachable through this API.

items.subject: Document 2.19 codec
items.resolution: Both document versions are supported; preserving source and imported-library versions is an explicit contract.

items.subject: Script 2.11 headers
items.resolution: Published scripts remain supported; the header compatibility set is independent of document versions.

items.subject: Conversation v1/v2 records
items.resolution: Session::open already upgrades to v3 at the read boundary while preserving drafts and native session continuity.

items.subject: Original-less attachment records
items.resolution: Old records retain only the normalized PNG; inventing original metadata would misrepresent retained data.

items.subject: Owner-less checkpoint records
items.resolution: Document paths cannot be reconstructed from namespace hashes; conservative retention protects unknown historical assets.

items.subject: Browser scope v1
items.resolution: Missing URL ownership is semantically meaningful; promotion to v2 requires explicit captured authority.

items.subject: Native dependency hash migrations
items.resolution: Localize reviewed legacy hash bridges in migrations.rs; preserve exact compiler and flag checks because expiry is unproven.

items.subject: Legacy cache keys
items.resolution: Legacy lookup still verifies source, recipe and dep-info; retention must not discard a distinct compiler context without replacement evidence.

items.subject: Previous release recipe
items.resolution: Move the single reviewed transition into migrations.rs while retaining debug-only reuse and old-release exclusion.

items.subject: Preview timing v1/v2
items.resolution: The measurement tool accepts arbitrary candidate binaries, so old format readers remain a live feature.

items.subject: Pagination duplication
items.resolution: MCP list_components now uses query::page_offset; keep existing stored/project cursor wire formats. Windows cross-target compilation also verifies the shared Job implementation; the browser worker result is explicitly typed.

items.subject: Node-query validation and filtering
items.resolution: Share page/address validation and NodeFilter, with one lowercase query per request.

items.subject: Canonical JSON hashing
items.resolution: Share document::canonical_hash across operations, bindings and script contexts; preserve the distinct CI cache wire encoder.

items.subject: Digest hex encoding
items.resolution: Share document::digest_hex across in-memory and streaming hashes without altering input bytes. Transcript, deletion-inventory and layout identities also use the shared byte-to-hex helper.

items.subject: Bounded file reads
items.resolution: Use one cancellable chunk reader; preserve each caller's size limit, symlink policy and error category.

items.subject: Lock retry loops
items.resolution: Registry leases and Store locks differ in cancellation, errors and waiting notifications; a shared loop would need policy switches without reducing ownership complexity.

items.subject: Windows job ownership
items.resolution: Share job creation, limits and worker join; preserve prefixes, non-inheritable ownership and limited join rights.

items.subject: ACP startup framing and stderr
items.resolution: Share the private 13-byte protocol and gated relay, preserving OS-specific magic and phase mapping.

items.subject: Unix owner watchdog
items.resolution: Use OwnerWatch for the same EOF observation and race-safe process-group binding.

items.subject: Component and variable lookup
items.resolution: Share namespace traversal and ambiguity handling; preserve runtime-reference and local-name precedence.

items.subject: Literal property classification
items.resolution: Share the base literal-property set while retaining resolution-only exceptions.

items.subject: Serialization budgets
items.resolution: Share allocation-free byte counting and early-abort serialization while retaining distinct caller budgets and errors. Node-reference and CLI layout limits use the same allocation-free size counter; CST source-span lengths remain unchanged.

items.subject: Project responsibilities
items.resolution: Separate capture, configuration/font handling and resolution without changing public methods or snapshot ownership.
items.retained_alternative: Keep Project as the owner of shared snapshots and budgets; modules isolate phases without duplicating that ownership.

items.subject: Copier state and namespace mapping
items.resolution: Group reuse indexes and budgets in reuse::State; share authored-key-first alias entries across compositions.
items.retained_alternative: Keep one Copier lifetime and shared allocation budget so recursive imports preserve ID and path reuse.

items.subject: Operation batch state
items.resolution: Batch owns one transaction state and final validation; import::Request groups operation arguments.

items.subject: Raster planning
items.resolution: RasterPlan owns input validation and dimensions before drawing allocation; retain the proven recording and compositing pipeline.
items.retained_alternative: Keep the proven pixel recording and compositing order; the plan isolates validation and allocation without changing rendering semantics.

items.subject: TUI agent state
items.resolution: Group negotiated agent settings in Status and use Pending/Reported to represent configuration receipt.
items.retained_alternative: Preview, camera and modal states have independent asynchronous lifecycles; a single App-wide enum would obscure valid concurrent states.

items.subject: TUI key routing
items.resolution: Separate priority routing from cancellation, permission, help, search, prompt and panel handlers.

items.subject: Argument-heavy contexts
items.resolution: Use shader::Request, ExpansionPass, ConversationChannels and import::Request while preserving public wrappers.

items.subject: Configuration font state
items.resolution: Share FontSources verification across user and project snapshots; retain public fields.

items.subject: Document reparsing and revisions
items.resolution: Cache revision at parse time; retain sequential parsing because later operations observe changed IDs and JSONC positions.
items.retained_alternative: Keep sequential parsing because subsequent operations use updated IDs, indexes and JSONC spans; cache repeated revision hashing instead.

items.subject: MCP catalogue and capabilities
items.resolution: Centralize names, scopes, effects and dispatch types; cache immutable schemas; advertise actual supported script headers.

items.subject: CI selection and stages
items.resolution: Separate selection rules and stage execution; map extracted modules to their previous consumer and runtime gates.

items.subject: Dynamic cache ownership
items.resolution: Keep entries, LRU order and invalidation under one Cache, with shared page shutdown and executable resolution.

items.subject: Internal worker dispatch
items.resolution: Read the worker argument once and share exit handling; preserve pre-initialization dispatch and private image errors.

items.subject: Large test modules
items.resolution: Split TUI and CI tests by feature, retaining test coverage and the TUI fully qualified test names used by CI. Fixed existing geometry-sensitive TUI fixtures by explicitly selecting their intended panel ratios; native image placement checks verify a full-image crop.

verification.notes: Local Chromium 156; isolated settings. Includes cancellation, retained page contexts, cache expiry, independent process expiry and software WebGL.

Official Rust 1.99.1. Compiles byte-identical agent/CDP supervisor source files and shared process_job code with their dependencies; not a full application build or Windows execution. Added explicit Result<bool> to the browser worker closure after this check exposed missing type inference.
Includes the independently committed document-picker overlay and background agent preparation.
The nonblocking event accessor added by concurrent TUI work is now compiled only with the tui feature; its only caller belongs to that feature.

notes: No local installed executable is replaced.
Concurrent document-picker UI and development-profile changes belong to separate work.
Prepared local fish and GNU tar binaries for shell completion and archive tests without altering installed applications.

review.method: Independent source and caller reviews of each scope, plus source-body comparisons for moved code.
confirmed_contracts: All 22 MCP tool names, schema input types and descriptions match the baseline.
MCP document scopes, mutation annotations and revision-exclusion rules match the baseline.
All 43 TUI tests retain their names and coverage.
The obsolete CI failed-platform test was replaced by coverage for extracted-module consumer selection.
Project method moves preserve bodies; component/variable lookup preserves priority.
Unix and Windows owner cleanup ordering and startup framing preserve their platform-specific contracts.
Exact supervisor source copies compile for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu with official Rust 1.99.1; no Windows runtime execution is claimed.
limitations: The macOS host cannot execute Windows binaries. Windows supervisor modules are separately checked for target compilation where available.

known_limitations.notes: The baseline and refactored application produce the same actual hash in this local Skia environment. No golden value was changed. The complete suite is not claimed to pass.

known_limitations.status: cross-target supervisor compilation only; native Windows execution not performed

integration.notes: Preserve the independently committed document-picker overlay and background agent preparation. The only merge conflict combines deferred setup with ConversationChannels; agent/main/TUI merged contents were checked against the prior combined worktree.
